correctness.rationale: The joint count (5) is a disjoint combinatorial bijection. Pair-fusion events have probabilities S(n-1,k)/S(n,k) and S(n-2,k)/S(n,k), with exactly one squared indicator, proving (1). Substitution S(n,2)=2^(n-1)-1 and F_{n+1}-2F_n=(n-1)(n-3) gives exact sharp sign. A one-doubleton partition proves (3), and conditioned independent k-box allocations with P(non-surjective)<=k(1-1/k)^n bound covariance error by 3n^2 P(non-surjective). Actual standalone checker passed 4,746 assertions over independent RGS enumerations for n=2,...,9 and exact arithmetic up to n=149. Finite checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: Two-tag block sizes are the natural smallest nontrivial dependence observable for exchangeable random clusters. Their covariance can be positive under coarse two-block conditioning and strictly negative under a single-pair perturbation of the discrete partition; the exact n=6 onset and persistence as n grows at fixed k give a qualitative finite-to-asymptotic account. This is more than routine table recomputation, while not asserting all-k classification or any downstream theorem.
